name: Iguana (SnellerInc)
workload: SIMD (AVX-512 VBMI2) decompression of an LZ-style format with entropy coding disabled, compared with LZ4 decompression.
claimed_speedup: Decompresses about 33% faster than LZ4 with entropy coding disabled (snippet of HN thread 'Iguana: fast SIMD-optimized decompression'; not verified on the repo).
hardware: Needs AVX-512 VBMI2 (Ice Lake, Tiger Lake, AMD Zen 4) per HN snippet; CPU model not stated
tradeoffs: Requires AVX-512 VBMI2 hardware. Repo is a bare C++ port with a README of one line, CMake and VS project files, test input and main.cpp; no documented API or format spec seen.
caveats: Snippet only: the Sneller blog post and the HN thread are blocked in this environment, and the repo README and file list carry no benchmark numbers. The 33% figure is a search-result snippet, so treat as unverified. TurboBench lists the ClickHouse fork with the comment 'Not reliable'. Fork ClickHouse/iguana exists with ClickHouse-specific changes (CHANGES.ClickHouse.md); not reported separately.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch (site news.ycombinator.com) 'Show HN LZ4 decompression AVX-512 OR SIMD OR GPU OR Rust OR Zig faster than reference lz4 implementation' surfaced thread 'Iguana: fast SIMD-optimized decompression'; repo found via github.com/SnellerInc org page.

verification.tier_reason: The SnellerInc/iguana repo has a one-line README ('A C iguana compression port'), no benchmark code and no numbers. The 30-33% faster-than-LZ4 figure is known only from HN/encode.su search snippets and refers to Sneller's original Go+AVX-512 assembly implementation, not to this repo. In this repo, iguana/decoder.cpp's decoder::decompress starts with IGUANA_UNIMPLEMENTED, the ans1/ans32/ans_nibble decode branches are also IGUANA_UNIMPLEMENTED with the Go code left in /*TODO*/ comments, and no file checked (decoder.cpp, ans1.cpp, ans32.cpp, ans_nibble.cpp, platform.h) has any _mm512/AVX-512 intrinsics.
verification.notes: Rejected for invalid evidence under the harness rule: the repo's own code contradicts the claim (the decoder is unimplemented and has no SIMD). If the orchestrator wants Iguana listed, the right target is the original Go+asm implementation in SnellerInc/sneller (its path was not found at ion/zion/iguana, iguana/ or compr/iguana) or the ClickHouse fork. Even then, ClickHouse PR #107560 measured it slower than ZSTD(3) on decompression. License Apache-2.0, 3 stars, 76 commits, last commit 2023-11-03, all confirmed.
verification.reject_reason: other: invalid evidence; the repo's own code contradicts the claim (the C++ port's decoder is unimplemented and has no AVX-512 code), and the only numbers are search snippets about the separate Go/assembly implementation

name: NZ1 (NanoZip 1)
baseline: lz4 (also compared with zstd and ZIP)
workload: Not stated; README performance table only
claimed_speedup: README: NZ1 about 58% ratio, 2.8 GB/s compress and 4.2 GB/s decompress on x86 AVX2; comparison table lists LZ4 ~80% ratio, 0.7 GB/s compress, 5 GB/s decompress; Zstd ~60%, 0.5 GB/s, 1.5 GB/s; ZIP ~65%, 0.12 GB/s, 0.25 GB/s (so claimed faster than LZ4 at compression and with a better ratio, slower than LZ4 at decompression)
tradeoffs: ~500 line C99 library with AVX2/SSE2/NEON paths and CRC32 validation; configurable window 1 KB to 1 MB; aimed at embedded use.
caveats: No benchmark code, no dataset, no CPU, no compiler or flags; the LZ4, Zstd and ZIP rows look like generic typical figures rather than measurements (LZ4 at 80% ratio is not a normal result for LZ4 on text); a LZ4 'ratio' of 80% versus NZ1 58% is not explained. Same author as stb-zip, whose fast path was previously found to compute a different checksum. Keep as low-confidence claim; not independently verified; I did not read nz1.c.

verification.tier_reason: README.txt lists NZ1 2.8/4.2 GB/s against LZ4 0.7/5 GB/s, Zstd 0.5/1.5 GB/s and ZIP 0.12/0.25 GB/s, but the repo contains no code that runs LZ4, Zstd or zlib, no dataset, CPU or flags; the only measured numbers (tests.txt, produced by the main() in nz1.c) are 29.31 MB/s compress and 30.99 MB/s decompress on a 1 MiB repeating alphabet, roughly 100x below the README claim. With no measured comparison against any baseline the record cannot sit above D.
verification.notes: Read nz1.c (586 lines) and tests.txt: the only real measurement is the author's own 29-31 MB/s run, and nothing in the repo times LZ4/Zstd/ZIP, so the README comparison table is invalid evidence in the same family as the stb-zip precedent. If the orchestrator keeps it under keep-and-document, it belongs at tier D with the caveats above. Metadata checked: MIT, 35 stars, 4 forks, 7 commits, last commit 2025-08-26 (stale), not a fork.
verification.reject_reason: other: invalid evidence - the README speed and LZ4/Zstd/ZIP comparison table has no measurement behind it and is contradicted by the repo's own benchmark output and code
